title: Manga: From Old Picture Scrolls to New Global Hits

cover.alt: Two adults compare an old animal scroll, a printed comic, and a tablet in a sunlit illustration studio.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Japanese comics called manga are read by millions of people around the world. They began hundreds of years ago and changed a lot over time. You will learn where manga started, how it grew, who reads it, and how you can read it today.

blocks.title: Before You Begin
blocks.intro: Think about these questions before you read.

items.prompt: Have you ever seen a manga or a comic book? What did it look like?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: Yes, I saw one at a bookshop. The pictures were black and white and the characters had big eyes.
items.explanation: Why do you think people enjoy reading stories with pictures?

blocks.title: Early Illustrated Roots
paragraphs: These old works are manga's early illustrated roots. Manga has very old roots in Japan. Around the year 1200, artists drew funny animal pictures on long paper scrolls. These scrolls are called Chōjū-giga, which means 'animal caricatures.' Frogs and rabbits wrestle and play like humans. Many people call Chōjū-giga the oldest manga.

About 600 years later, an artist named Katsushika Hokusai used the word 'manga' for the first time. In 1814, he published a book of sketches called Hokusai Manga. The book showed people, animals, plants, and landscapes. Hokusai drew over 3,000 pictures across 15 volumes. His work showed that a series of pictures could tell many ideas together.

items.prompt: What are two things that Chōjū-giga and Hokusai Manga have in common?
items.answer: Both are very old Japanese works with many pictures. Both are important early examples that helped give manga its roots.
items.explanation:
Chōjū-giga used animal pictures on scrolls around 1200, and Hokusai Manga used thousands of sketches in 1814. Both showed that pictures could carry ideas and stories.

Which of these two works surprises you more? Why?

blocks.title: Modern Manga Development
paragraphs: This modern manga development changed picture stories in Japan. Modern manga began after World War Two. American comic books came to Japan, and Japanese artists saw a new way to tell stories. One young artist changed everything.

Osamu Tezuka published New Treasure Island in 1947. This comic book told an adventure story with fast camera-like angles, close-up faces, and action scenes. Young readers loved it. About 400,000 copies sold quickly. Many other artists copied Tezuka's style. He later created Astro Boy, a story about a robot boy, which also became a famous anime. Tezuka is often called 'the God of Manga.' His work set the visual style that most people think of as manga today.

items.prompt: Why was New Treasure Island important for manga?
items.answer: It introduced a new visual storytelling style with dynamic angles and close-up faces. It sold about 400,000 copies and inspired many other manga artists to follow Tezuka's approach.
items.explanation:
Before Tezuka, manga did not use cinematic techniques. New Treasure Island changed what manga looked like and how popular it could be.

Can you think of a book, film, or game that changed something big in its field?

blocks.title: Wide Manga Audiences
paragraphs: New kinds of stories helped manga reach wide manga audiences. Not everyone wants the same story. Manga publishers learned this and made different types for different readers.

In the 1950s and 1960s, some artists wanted more serious stories for adults. They created a style called gekiga, which means 'dramatic pictures.' Gekiga stories showed real life problems, crime, and social issues. At the same time, publishers started making manga for girls. This type is called shōjo manga. Shōjo stories focused on feelings, friendships, and romance. The pictures used large expressive eyes and soft lines.

Today, there is manga for children, teenagers, men, women, and older adults. Each type has its own name and its own magazine. This is one reason why manga became so popular — almost everyone can find a story made for them.

items.prompt: How are gekiga and shōjo manga different from each other?
items.answer: Gekiga focuses on serious adult themes like real life problems and crime. Shōjo focuses on feelings and relationships and uses soft, expressive art. They target very different readers.
items.explanation:
Both types came from publishers wanting to reach new audiences, but they went in opposite directions in tone and art style.

Which type of story do you prefer — serious drama or emotional relationships? Why?

blocks.title: Global Digital Reach
paragraphs: Official online services now give manga global digital reach. Manga moved from Japan to the whole world, first through anime and then through digital technology.

When Astro Boy became a TV anime in 1963, international audiences discovered Tezuka's characters. Other manga titles followed. Later, publishers began translating manga into English, French, Spanish, and many other languages.

Now readers can use digital platforms to read manga online. Some publishers release new chapters at the same time in Japan and in other countries. This is called a simultaneous release. KADOKAWA, one of Japan's biggest manga publishers, offers simultaneous English digital chapter releases through its services. Readers anywhere in the world can follow their favourite story the same week it comes out in Japan.

items.prompt: What does 'simultaneous release' mean, and why is it good for international readers?
items.answer: A simultaneous release means a new chapter comes out in Japan and in other countries at the same time. International readers do not have to wait weeks or months for a translation.
items.explanation:
Before digital simultaneous releases, fans outside Japan often waited a long time and sometimes read unofficial copies. Official simultaneous releases changed that.

Do you use any app or website to read or watch content from other countries?

blocks.title: Manga Publishing and Visual Language
paragraphs: Manga publishing with visual language keeps a story moving. Manga uses special pictures and publishing tools to keep readers excited.

One important visual tool is speed lines. These are thin lines drawn around a moving object or a character's face. Researchers studied speed lines and found that they make readers feel movement and direction, even in a still picture. A punch with speed lines feels fast. A running character feels real.
Manga also uses written sound effects called onomatopoeia directly on the page. A loud bang might appear as a large bold word inside the panel.

To keep readers buying, manga stories are published in chapters inside weekly or monthly magazines. After enough chapters are printed, they are collected into a book called a tankōbon. A cliffhanger ending — a moment where something exciting happens right before the chapter stops — makes readers come back for the next issue. These tools work together to make manga a habit, not just a hobby.

images.alt: At an illustrator’s desk, one red ball has speed lines and motion echoes while an identical ball without lines looks still.

blocks.title: Check: Manga Publishing and Visual Language

items.prompt: Name two tools manga artists use to make stories feel exciting. What does each one do?
items.answer: Speed lines make still pictures feel like movement. A cliffhanger ending stops the chapter at an exciting moment so readers want to buy the next issue.
items.explanation:
These tools work at different levels — speed lines work inside a single panel, while cliffhangers work across whole chapters and issues.

Can you think of a story you read or watched that had a strong cliffhanger? What happened?

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: Think about everything you read and answer in your own words.

items.prompt: You have read about manga from ancient scrolls to digital chapters today. Which part of manga history do you think is most important? Why?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: I think Osamu Tezuka's work was most important because New Treasure Island created the visual style that all modern manga uses. Without his ideas, manga might not have become so popular worldwide.
items.explanation:
There is no single correct answer. Strong answers pick one moment or idea and give a clear reason connected to facts from the article.

Is there something about manga you want to explore more after reading this?
